lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Circles, Angles, Area, and Surface Area
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: area of circles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: A circle has a radius of 6 ft. What is its exact area?

steps: Area is π times the radius squared: A = πr².
Square the radius: 6² = 36, so A = 36π ft².

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle's radius equals its circumference divided by 2π. A circle has a circumference of 25/2π cm. Use this relationship to find the circle's exact area, as a multiple of π.
Two angles are complementary. One angle measures 10°. What is the measure of the other angle?
Two lines intersect, forming vertical angles that measure (6x + 5)° and (2x + 53)°. Vertical angles are congruent. Find the value of x and the measure of the angles.
Two angles are supplementary. Their measures are (2x + 9)° and (5x + 31)°. Find the value of x and the measure of each angle.
Three angles lie along a straight line and measure 60°, 79°, 7°, and x°. What is the value of x?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A room shaped like an L is made from a 10-by-15 rectangle with a 2-by-3 rectangular corner cut out. What is the area of the room, in square units?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 92 square units and a width of 6 units. What is its exact length, in units?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 5, width 11, and height 3 1/2 (all in units). What is its exact surface area, in square units?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
